024.t: The Internet, DNS and Cloud Storage
o: Define the Internet as a worldwide network of networks.
Describe how DNS finds an IP address for a domain name.
Explain advantages and risks of cloud-based services.
c: The Internet is a worldwide set of interconnected computer networks where clients can request resources from servers.
The Domain Name System uses distributed servers to look up IP addresses associated with domain names.
Cloud storage puts files on remote servers; cloud software and processing also provide services using remote computing resources.
Cloud services support access from different devices, but depend on connectivity, service availability and secure access.

m.title: Find the web server
m.q: A pupil enters a website's domain name in a browser. Describe how DNS helps them reach its web server. [4 marks]
st: The pupil begins with a readable domain name, not the server's numeric network address.
The device queries a DNS service to find the matching IP address [1].
DNS looks up the domain [1] and returns the IP address to the client [1].
The browser connects to the web server using that address [1]. Check the sequence.

w: A visitor enters the name of a local museum website. Describe the DNS lookup and connection in four stages. [4 marks]
Client asks DNS for an address [1]; DNS finds an IP address linked to the name [1]; returns the IP address [1]; browser connects to the web server [1].
A student stores revision notes on a remote service. Explain one advantage and one disadvantage. [4 marks]
Notes can be accessed from different connected devices [1], enabling work at home or school [1]. Internet/provider availability is needed [1], so outages can block access [1].
Explain the difference between a client and a server when watching a web-hosted tutorial. [4 marks]
The student's device is a client [1] requesting the tutorial [1]; the remote server hosts/provides the content [1] and responds to the request [1].
wSteps: Begin with the user's typed domain name.
Client makes a DNS request [1]; DNS finds the matching IP [1].
DNS returns address [1]; browser uses it to reach server [1].
Client asks DNS for an address [1]; DNS finds an IP address linked to the name [1]; returns the IP address [1]; browser connects to the web server [1].
Use one benefit and one drawback linked to remote storage.
Access from multiple devices [1]; dependence on a connection [1].
Convenient at multiple locations [1] but unavailable if the service is down [1].
Notes can be accessed from different connected devices [1], enabling work at home or school [1]. Internet/provider availability is needed [1], so outages can block access [1].
Decide who requests and who supplies the video.
Server: provides remote content and response [2].
The student's device is a client [1] requesting the tutorial [1]; the remote server hosts/provides the content [1] and responds to the request [1].

k.q: Model a DNS lookup using known demonstration values; no real network request is made.
p: Add print("Lookup complete") at the end.
k.a:
Initially: library.example; 192.0.2.77.

Extended OCR ERL:
domain = "museum.example"
ip = "192.0.2.77"
print(domain)
print(ip)
print("Lookup complete")

The address uses a reserved documentation range. The script simulates an answer, not DNS.

State one purpose of DNS. [2 marks]

Source: Adapted from your Paper 1 revision booklet, 1.3.1.
It looks up an IP address [1] associated with a requested domain name [1].

A pupil cannot open a cloud document during an Internet outage. Explain a benefit and a limitation of cloud storage. [4 marks]

Source: Original J277-style question; not a past-paper original.
Benefit: access remotely from different devices [1], allowing work at school/home [1]. Limitation: requires availability of connection/provider [1], so data may be temporarily inaccessible [1].

Describe how DNS, a client and a web server interact when opening a web page. [6 marks]

Source: Original J277-style question; not a past-paper original.
Client starts with name [1] and requests DNS lookup [1]; DNS locates address [1] and returns IP [1]; client contacts server [1], which returns requested content [1].

r: State what a NIC allows a computer to do. [1 mark]
Connect to a network to send/receive data [1].
Explain why large cache may improve performance.
More frequently used data/instructions fit in fast cache, reducing RAM access.
Why is a thermostat an embedded system?
Its controller is built into a larger device for one specific job.
A LAN printer works but a website cannot load. What might need checking, and why?
Check the router/Internet link because the LAN may still allow local printing while the WAN/Internet route fails.
